subject.title: [Bug]: Enabling Codex plugin causes Runtime to switch to OpenAI Codex and ignore configured primary model, resulting in GPT-5.4-nano TPM failures

question: Should #99449 be fixed as a narrow stale OpenAI/Codex session override repair for non-OpenAI primaries, folded into the broader #87957 session-state resolver, or treated as expected explicit `/model openai` behavior with better diagnostics?
rationale: Source shows DeepSeek should not be claimed directly by Codex, but the report combines Codex hot reload, persisted selected/runtime model state, and an explicit `/model openai` clarification, so automation should not choose the permanent session-state contract alone.

options.title: Fix narrow route drift first
options.body: Repair stale auto OpenAI/Codex session pins for non-OpenAI primaries now, then leave #87957 for the broader resolver cleanup.

options.title: Fold into #87957
options.body: Make #87957 the canonical owner and copy this DeepSeek/Codex hot-reload scenario into its acceptance criteria before closing this issue later.

options.title: Keep OpenAI selection expected
options.body: If maintainers decide the report is only explicit `/model openai`, preserve Codex-for-OpenAI behavior and improve status/doctor diagnostics instead of changing routing.

recommendation.title: Fix narrow route drift first
recommendation.body: Repair stale auto OpenAI/Codex session pins for non-OpenAI primaries now, then leave #87957 for the broader resolver cleanup.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest recent history across OpenAI provider identity, Codex doctor ownership, and agent runtime/session-state boundaries involved in this decision.
